result:
**Opening argument for c = 1/18**

Debater A's value, 1/25, would require every admissible K₅-free graph with α = o(n) to be bipartizable after deleting only n²/25 + o(n²) edges. The three-part Bollobás–Erdős construction refutes that.

**Lower bound (c ≥ 1/18).** Split the vertex set into three parts V₁, V₂, V₃ of size n/3. Place a K₄-free Bollobás–Erdős graph of density 1/2 + o(1) between each pair of parts. Since any K₅ would need four vertices in two of the three parts, and each part-pair is K₄-free, the graph is K₅-free. Its independence number is o(n), a standard property of Bollobás–Erdős graphs.

Now take any bipartition (A, B). Pigeonhole forces at least one pair Vᵢ, Vⱼ to have its two sides mostly on the same side of the bipartition. That pair then has about half its (n/3)² cross-edges inside a single class, so roughly (1/2)(n/3)² = n²/18 + o(n²) edges must be deleted. Hence no constant below 1/18 works.

**Upper bound (c ≤ 1/18).** The sharp Ramsey–Turán stability theorem for K₅-free graphs with α(G) = o(n) gives β(G) ≤ n²/18 + o(n²) for every such G. This matches the construction, so the smallest valid constant is exactly 1/18.

Debater A must either exhibit a K₅-free, o(n)-independence graph needing fewer than n²/18 deletions, which the construction above rules out, or explain why the pigeonhole step fails. I see no such failure.
